notes: Majiabang culture of the Lake Tai region; infobox 'Dates: 5000-3350 BC' (text '5000 BC to 3300 BC'), with the later part 'a separate cultural phase, referred to as the Songze culture'. The Songze page dates the Songze 3800-3300 BCE and calls it 'the successor of the Majiabang culture', so the Majiabang is cut at 3800 and handed to the Songze (the infobox end 3350 is the end of the whole tradition, a disagreement). Extent: 'primarily around Lake Tai west of modern Shanghai', 'occupied the Yangtze River Delta', 'spread throughout southern Jiangsu and Zhejiang north of Hangzhou Bay'; type site Weidun at Changzhou, Jiangsu; Luojiajiao '5300 to 4900 cal. BC'. The shape is Lake Tai + Changzhou + Shanghai + Jiaxing + Wuxi, without the Ningbo disc of the Hemudu; confidence 2 (year from the page, region the dossier's reading). Pudong and downtown Shanghai 'were still part of the East China Sea'; the land cells drawn there are the gazetteer's present coast. The page's two period labels ('during the period 5000 to 4300 BC and 4300 to 3500 BC') are not tied to named phases and are not used. The Dawenkou is the northern neighbour ('the northern Jiangsu sites were of the Dawenkou culture'); the Hemudu is the southern, coexisting culture. No area figure.
